I ported the C++ calculator to Zig in `src/main.zig`. It passes all 6 example cases in `node check.mjs`, plus a few small unit tests I added.

To check it beyond the examples, I built the original C++ version and fed both programs the same three large generated inputs, about 294,000 lines each, and their output was byte-for-byte identical. The inputs included the checker's own expression generator, random junk lines (stray characters, tabs, `\r`), parentheses nested 500,000 deep, a million unary
